feedback.problem: If $\,T\,$ is a linear transformation and $\,T([\begin{aligned}8 \\ 16\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}28 \\ -20\end{aligned}]$, then find $\,T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $\,T\,$ is a linear transformation, it must satisfy $\,T(kv)=kT(v).$ Noting that $[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 16\end{aligned}]=4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T([\begin{aligned}8 \\ 16\end{aligned}]) & =T(4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}])=4T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since we're told that 

$$
T([\begin{aligned}8 \\ 16\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}28 \\ -20\end{aligned}],
$$

we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}4T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}28 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]) & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}28 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\ T([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]) & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
